title: Aromatic Anti-Inflammatory Egyptian Chicken Tagine
description: This pungent and gooey Egyptian dish is perfect for a post-workout meal, featuring madras paste and steam to reduce inflammation. The combination of spices and herbs creates a unique flavor profile.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in the bottom of a clay or ceramic tagine or a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is softened and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in the madras paste, turmeric, cumin, and coriander and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken to the pot and cook until it is browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the chicken broth, dried apricots, and browned chicken to the pot, then cover the tagine or Dutch oven with a lid.
Transfer the pot to the oven and cook at 300 degrees Fahrenheit for 30 minutes, then reduce the heat to 250 degrees Fahrenheit and cook for an additional 20 minutes.
Remove the pot from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes, then serve the tagine hot, garnished with chopped fresh cilantro or parsley.
Serve the tagine over couscous or rice to soak up the flavorful sauce.
